title: Commercial friction contract
description: One COMMERCIAL-lane record: the buyer and payment trigger, the pricing model, the friction to buy, and the leading/decisive metric split, all as falsifiable hypotheses rather than one PAID_VALIDATED bit. Composes with `../productization-program.schema.json` (pol/productization-program/v1): this record is what a program's `lanes.commercial` object is produced from, and its own `authority.paid_truth` constant restates the parent's `authority.paid_truth: false` rather than redefining it. Every hypothesis-shaped field is closed with its own `falsifier`, so a claim without a stated way to prove it wrong cannot be represented at all. Six refusals are structural: a leading interest signal cannot stand in the decisive-metric slot; a claimed repeatable business requires at least two distinct payment events; a price cannot be reported without the buyer it binds to or without its delivery cost alongside it; a free-trial motion cannot leave post-trial friction unstated; and existing-subscription leverage is a closed pair of booleans with no room for a third key asserting one implies the other.

subject_commit.description: The exact commit this commercial record is bound to. A branch or tag fails the pattern, for the same reason the parent program schema pins its own subject: a record bound to a moving name describes whatever that name points at when somebody next reads it.

buyer_and_payment_trigger.description: Who pays, and the exact event that starts the payment obligation. Kept as one object because a trigger with no bound buyer is a mechanism with no economic actor.

buyer_ref.description: The economic decision-maker, named as a role or account type, not a person.

payment_trigger.description: The exact event that starts the payment obligation (e.g. seat activation, first successful run, invoice threshold crossed).

commercial_model.description: The four shapes this lane distinguishes. SERVICE_ASSISTED names a model where a person's labor is part of what is sold, not merely part of how it is delivered.

price_hypothesis.description: A price is only a claim about a named buyer. `buyer_ref` is required here, independently of `buyer_and_payment_trigger`, so a price cannot be stated with the buyer left as an assumption carried over from elsewhere. x-refusal-control PRICE_WITHOUT_BUYER: refused_by properties.price_hypothesis.required.

price_value_hypothesis.description: The hypothesised price point and unit, e.g. '$29/seat/month' or '$0.02/call above the free tier'.

delivery_cost_hypothesis.description: What it costs to actually deliver the priced unit. Required at the top level alongside `price_hypothesis` so a gross price cannot be reported with no companion cost figure next to it. x-refusal-control GROSS_VALUE_WITHOUT_DELIVERY_COST: refused_by required (top level, the `delivery_cost_hypothesis` entry).

sales_motion.description: How the sale actually happens. A FREE_TRIAL_LED motion carries a conditional requirement below: it may not omit `friction_after_trial_ends`. x-refusal-control FREE_TRIAL_AS_LOW_FRICTION_BY_DEFAULT: refused_by properties.sales_motion.allOf[0].then.required.

integration_burden.description: The new-account, API-key and integration burden the buyer clears before the priced unit does anything for them.

existing_subscription_leverage.description: A consumer subscription and an API/integration entitlement are two separate booleans, never merged into one. Closed with no third key, so no invented field can assert that one implies the other. x-refusal-control EXISTING_SUBSCRIPTION_ASSUMED_API_ENTITLEMENT: refused_by properties.existing_subscription_leverage.additionalProperties.

commercial_metrics.description: A leading metric and a decisive metric, reported separately so neither can be silently promoted into the other. x-refusal-control INTEREST_AS_PAYMENT: refused_by $defs.decisive_metric.properties.metric_class.enum, which excludes INTEREST_SIGNAL, USAGE_SIGNAL and CONVERSION_SIGNAL from the decisive slot.

repeatable_commercial_claim.description: `claimed: true` names an assertion that this is a repeatable business, not a one-off payment. That assertion requires at least two distinct payment events below it. x-refusal-control ONE_PAYMENT_AS_REPEATABLE_BUSINESS: refused_by properties.repeatable_commercial_claim.allOf[0].then.properties.distinct_payment_events.minItems.

authority.description: Restates, not redefines, the parent program's `authority.paid_truth` constant. This record can carry a payment hypothesis and a falsifier; it cannot itself be the thing that makes paid_truth true.

evidence_class.description: HYPOTHESIS: authored by this method, not yet tested. SOURCE_STATEMENT: restated from an external artifact at its exact identity, per the SOURCE lane. OBSERVED_TRANSACTION: bound to a PAYMENT_RECORD or REPEATED_PAYMENT_SERIES receipt in the parent program's evidence ladder. A value of this class here is not itself that receipt.

falsifier.description: What observation would prove this value wrong. Required so the hypothesis and its falsifier are one unit; a value with no stated falsifier is not representable.

decisive_metric.description: The decisive slot's metric_class is narrower than the leading slot's: only TRANSACTION_SIGNAL and REPEATED_TRANSACTION_SIGNAL are admissible. An interest, usage or conversion signal cannot be filed here.

buyer_and_payment_trigger.buyer_ref: solo operator on the free tier of a synthetic note-taking helper
buyer_and_payment_trigger.payment_trigger: monthly note volume crosses the free-tier cap for two consecutive months
buyer_and_payment_trigger.falsifier: if operators who cross the cap downgrade their usage rather than upgrade, the trigger does not convert and is not a payment trigger at all

price_hypothesis.buyer_ref: solo operator on the free tier of a synthetic note-taking helper
price_hypothesis.price_value_hypothesis: $0.01 per note above 500 notes/month, billed monthly
price_hypothesis.falsifier: if fewer than one in twenty free-tier operators ever crosses 500 notes/month, the metered unit is priced on volume nobody reaches

delivery_cost_hypothesis.value: storage and embedding cost per note is hypothesised at $0.002, leaving a $0.008 margin per metered note
delivery_cost_hypothesis.falsifier: if measured per-note infra cost exceeds $0.01, the metered price is sold below delivery cost

friction_after_trial_ends.value: at 500 notes the operator sees a blocking upgrade screen with no data export offered first
friction_after_trial_ends.falsifier: if operators abandon at the blocking screen rather than upgrade, the trial converted attention, not payment

sales_motion.falsifier: if operators self-serve past the cap without ever seeing anyone from the vendor, DIRECT_SALES is misclassified against actual behaviour

integration_effort.value: signup plus one OAuth consent screen, no API key needed for the note-taking UI path
integration_effort.falsifier: if the OAuth consent screen has a measured abandonment rate above 40%, the burden is mis-stated as low

existing_subscription_leverage.falsifier: if a bundled consumer subscription is later found to include API quota for this integration, this pair must be re-read, not assumed unchanged

time_to_value_before_payment.value: first useful note-recall result inside 3 minutes of signup, hypothesised from the onboarding flow's step count
time_to_value_before_payment.falsifier: if a timed session shows first useful recall taking longer than 10 minutes, the stated time-to-value is wrong

implementation_support_burden.value: zero-touch self-serve; no implementation call is scheduled into the onboarding path
implementation_support_burden.falsifier: if a support ticket volume analysis shows most new accounts opening a ticket before first payment, the burden is mis-stated as zero-touch

refund_cancellation_reversal_path.value: self-serve cancellation inside account settings; pro-rated refund on annual plans within 14 days
refund_cancellation_reversal_path.falsifier: if cancellation requires an email round-trip in practice, the self-serve claim is wrong

expansion_value.value: a second workspace seat is hypothesised to add $0.01/note at the same metered rate, no separate seat fee
expansion_value.falsifier: if multi-seat accounts show materially different metered usage per seat, the flat per-note expansion assumption is wrong

leading_metric.falsifier: if this count rises but the metered conversion rate below stays flat, the leading metric moved for reasons unrelated to payment

decisive_metric.metric_name: metered invoices paid in full within terms
decisive_metric.falsifier: if paid invoices trend downward while the leading metric trends upward, the two have decoupled and the leading metric no longer predicts the decisive one

kill_iterate_threshold.value: iterate if metered conversion of capped accounts stays under 2% after 90 days; kill if under 0.5% after 180 days
kill_iterate_threshold.falsifier: these thresholds are themselves a hypothesis about willingness to pay; a single cohort's result at one price point does not establish them as the right cutoffs

repeatable_commercial_claim.falsifier: no payment event has been observed yet for this synthetic subject; claimed stays false until at least two distinct payers are recorded

x-refusal-controls.refuses: INTEREST_AS_PAYMENT: an interest signal filed in the decisive-metric slot.

buyer_and_payment_trigger.falsifier: if operators downgrade instead of upgrading, no trigger exists

price_hypothesis.falsifier: if usage never crosses the cap, the price is untested

delivery_cost_hypothesis.falsifier: if measured cost exceeds price, margin is negative

sales_motion.falsifier: if a sales rep is observed closing deals, this is misclassified

integration_effort.falsifier: if signup abandonment is high, burden is understated

existing_subscription_leverage.falsifier: if entitlement is later found bundled, re-read this pair

time_to_value_before_payment.falsifier: if a timed session exceeds 10 minutes, this is wrong

implementation_support_burden.falsifier: if most accounts open a ticket first, this is wrong

refund_cancellation_reversal_path.falsifier: if cancellation needs an email round-trip, this is wrong

expansion_value.falsifier: if per-seat usage varies materially, this is wrong

leading_metric.falsifier: if signups rise with flat payment, the leading metric decoupled

decisive_metric.falsifier: if nobody who joins the waitlist ever pays, interest was never decisive

kill_iterate_threshold.falsifier: a single cohort does not establish this cutoff
